caption_review: None of the five captions merely repeats a title. They name the machine and frame (DIII-D 137D, DIII-D 146D, MAST 21978/35), the arm order, the residuals and convergence, the 21 shared flux levels with their values in Wb, the marker vocabulary including that hollow solved markers are exterior roots, and, for the three midplane figures, that the EFIT crosses and their local legend apply only to the left map-current panel. Those midplane captions match the picture: the EFIT key is drawn as an axes-local legend above the left panel and the two component panels carry no EFIT trace. The frame-137 poloidal caption's separation clause (closest centres 15.275 pt, 1.863 stroked marker diameters) is consistent with the render's 24 px nearest max/saddle spacing. It is silent on the solved minimum that overlaps a maximum in that same zoom, which is recorded as a finding against the figure.

0.reason: the base core counts are stated in the caption and table; a residual near-overprint of one maximum and one minimum on the superseded base panel does not hide the head result

1.reason: the separation check is a prototype guard; its marker-class limit is noted and the rendered panels were inspected

findings.summary: In the frame-137 base core zoom a filled solved maximum and a filled solved minimum stand with their centres about 2 px apart on the 1714x882 render, so the minimum's circle is covered by the maximum's triangle and only a crescent survives to its right (a 7x4 px fragment at x 622, y 639, against a 9 px circle drawn elsewhere in the same panel). The zoom therefore conceals the kind of one admitted in-plasma critical point: a reader sees a triangle with a blue bulge rather than a maximum standing beside a minimum. The panel's headline count is unaffected, since the four maxima (filled upward triangles) and the three saddles (crosses) are each separately visible and countable at about 24 px between nearest centres, which agrees with the caption's 15.275 pt; the caption's separation claim is correctly scoped to those seven points and does not cover the minimum.

The core-zoom separation guard inventories only markers it can classify by path vertex count, three for a maximum and twelve for a saddle, and it raises on any other filled marker instead of measuring it. Its check therefore passed at 1.863 marker diameters while the rendered panel still overprints a maximum and a minimum, because no minimum enters its pair list: it reports separation for the same seven points the caption names and cannot see the pair that actually collides. Extending the inventory to the solved minima the drawing code emits would make the guard fail on the state this render shows.

The frame-146 head core zoom carries no solved flux contour at all: its window holds only the dashed EFIT loop, the hollow EFIT maximum inside it, and the solved maximum marker drawn over a black EFIT-minimum square. A reader who opens the zoom for the held core's shape finds the EFIT core and the markers instead, and has to return to the full head panel, where the single-peaked held core is clear. The base zoom in the same figure is fully populated, and nothing on the panel signals the asymmetry.
